claims.text: The target WTaTiVZr HEA is equimolar, corresponding to approximately 20 at.% of each element.
The multiple principal refractory elements induce significant local lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr.
Local lattice distortions act as distributed barriers to dislocation motion.
Local lattice distortions facilitate dynamic dislocation mobility at high temperature.
Local lattice distortions facilitate dynamic dislocation recovery at high temperature.
The heterogeneous stress fields associated with lattice distortion promote dynamic dislocation climb.
The heterogeneous stress fields associated with lattice distortion promote dislocation cross-slip.
Solid-solution effects from the multiple refractory elements strengthen the HEA.
Enhanced high-temperature dislocation dynamics allow dislocations to bypass obstacles.
Dynamic recovery suppresses strain localization in the HEA.
Suppression of strain localization increases the HEA's plastic strain relative to pure tungsten.
Suppression of strain localization increases the HEA's toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The proposed dislocation mechanism delays catastrophic brittle fracture under sustained plasma-facing-component loading.
Under identical high-temperature testing, the HEA will have a lower yield strength than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature testing, the HEA will have significantly greater plastic strain than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature testing, the HEA will have significantly greater toughness than pure tungsten.
The HEA will exhibit higher dislocation mobility and more uniform plastic deformation than pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten will exhibit more localized strain, leading to premature crack formation.
Testing at 1000–1300 °C and a strain rate of about 10^-4 s^-1 is representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service conditions.
The proposed behavior is expected to apply only in the 1000–1300 °C slow-strain-rate regime and may not extend to radically different loading conditions.
